thread.title: Wall Street Keeps Missing The Target On Trade With China

author: Peter Tchir
title: Wall Street Keeps Missing The Target On Trade With China
text:
On Friday, U.S. stocks were hit as stories circulated that China may consider hitting U.S. tech companies with bans in retaliation for tariffs we have imposed.  So far I have not seen this story picked up by any major media source, but it was enough to help propel Apple Inc. (AAPL) down 4% on Friday and spark some analysis on what the implications could be. I continue to believe that there is too much attention on tariffs and not enough attention on what is really going on - which is a battle for Intellectual Property Rights and Reciprocal Access.
The U.S. is trying to protect the edge we currently have in Intellectual Property.  China is pushing hard for China 2025 .  The market acts surprised when stories circulate about China potentially taking steps to aid their technology firms, even though they have basically told us that is their plan.
China has laid out where they want to be and it is relatively easy to identify steps that might help them get there.
This is why Wall Street has gotten trade with China so wrong.

Every economist is trained to have a Pavlovian response to "Trade Wars" and that response is that they are always bad.
But why?  Is this really a "trade war" or is it about protecting intellectual property and creating consistent and reciprocal practices?  Hasn't there actually been a "trade war" going on for decades, but only one side was firing bullets?
